mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation (Enterprise Legal Person Business License)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) or the competent local Market Supervision Administration
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: PARALLEL MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE PATHS ONLY: (A) If the destination jurisdiction is a Hague Apostille Convention state: issue the certificate -> notarize with a PRC notary public -> obtain an Apostille from the Provincial Foreign Affairs Office -> transmit to the destination authority; do not add consular legalization. (B) If the destination jurisdiction is NOT an Apostille Convention state: issue the certificate -> notarize with a PRC notary public -> obtain certification from the Provincial Foreign Affairs Office -> obtain Consular Legalization from the embassy or consulate of the destination state in China; do not add an Apostille. Never combine Apostille and consular legalization sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (Enterprise Credit Information Public Report bearing an official seal)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) through the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: PARALLEL MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE PATHS ONLY: (A) For Hague Apostille Convention destination states: print the official Enterprise Credit Report -> notarize the printout -> obtain Apostille from the Provincial Foreign Affairs Office -> file with the destination authority. (B) For non-Apostille destination states: notarize the printout -> obtain Provincial Foreign Affairs Office certification -> obtain Consular Legalization from the destination state's consular post in China. Apostille and consular legalization are alternative routes and must never be chained.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and Power of Attorney authorizing the incorporation filer and the foreign shareholder representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of Directors and shareholders of the proposed Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Venture, notarized by a PRC notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: PARALLEL MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE PATHS ONLY: (A) For Hague Apostille states: execute the resolution/PoA -> notarize in China -> obtain Apostille from the Provincial Foreign Affairs Office -> deliver to the destination authority. (B) For non-Apostille states: execute the resolution/PoA -> notarize in China -> obtain Provincial Foreign Affairs Office certification -> obtain Consular Legalization at the destination state's embassy or consulate in China. Do not apply both procedures to the same document.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association and Joint Venture Contract
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Joint venture shareholders and legal representative, filed with SAMR and notarized for offshore use
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: PARALLEL MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE PATHS ONLY: (A) For Hague Apostille destination states: finalize the JV contract and articles -> notarize the signed copies -> obtain Apostille from the Provincial Foreign Affairs Office -> submit to the destination authority. (B) For non-Apostille destination states: notarize the signed copies -> obtain Provincial Foreign Affairs Office certification -> obtain Consular Legalization from the destination state's consular office in China. These two paths are mutually exclusive and may not be combined.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter (Good Standing Bank Letter from the foreign investor's or JV opening bank)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Commercial bank holding the JV's or the foreign shareholder's transaction account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: PARALLEL MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE PATHS ONLY: (A) For Hague Apostille states: issue the bank letter -> notarize the bank signature and seal before a PRC notary -> obtain Apostille from the Provincial Foreign Affairs Office -> forward to the destination authority. (B) For non-Apostille states: notarize the bank letter -> obtain Provincial Foreign Affairs Office certification -> obtain Consular Legalization from the destination state's embassy or consulate in China. Apostille and consular legalization are alternative authentication channels and must never be applied in sequence.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Before accepting any director, shareholder, or beneficial owner, the formation agent must run each identified individual and entity through the UN Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, and the People's Bank of China Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing Risk List. Enhanced due diligence is mandatory for politically exposed persons (PEPs), their family members, and close associates for 12 months after leaving office. Negative news, sanctions exposure, adverse media, and PEP status must be documented in a written risk memo; any hit blocks incorporation until legal clearance is issued by the compliance partner.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: SAMR National Enterprise Registration and Enterprise Name Reservation Service Platform (operated by the State Administration for Market Regulation)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: A Chinese company name must be in simplified Chinese characters and follow the four-tier sequence: (1) administrative division; (2) unique trade name; (3) industry or business characteristics; (4) legal form such as 'Limited Liability Company' or 'Co., Ltd.'. The Chinese trade name may be a phonetic transliteration of the foreign investor's name only if it is phonetically compatible and does not mislead the public. The foreign-language name may be filed in brackets for banking and commercial convenience but cannot replace the Chinese statutory name. Names with no distinctive element, names identical or similar to a prior registered name, and names implying state authorization will be rejected.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within five working days after rejection, the applicant may submit a written administrative reconsideration request to the market supervision authority at the next higher level, attaching the rejection notice, the reserved name proof, the four-part proposed name, and any prior trademark registration certificate. The reconsideration authority must issue a written decision within thirty days. If reconsideration fails, the applicant may file an administrative lawsuit in the competent people's court within six months. A name reservation may be extended for one additional thirty-day period before expiry if no third-party opposition has been registered.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Under Article 10 of the Company Law and SAMR registration rules, a Chinese limited liability company must maintain a registered business address that is a fixed physical place supported by a property ownership certificate or a lawful lease agreement. A purely virtual office or commercial mailbox is generally rejected by the State Taxation Administration for VAT and enterprise income tax address verification and by banks for corporate account opening due to on-site KYC and business-visit requirements. For the present low-risk market-research SaaS entity, a serviced office or co-working suite with a real three-month lease and physical staff presence may be accepted, but a postal mail-drop address alone is not permissible and will trigger enhanced scrutiny.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Inspection checklist: (i) registered address matches the lease or property certificate; (ii) company name plate is visibly installed; (iii) employees, directors, or the responsible person are present; (iv) business records, computers, and servers are physically located at the address; (v) utility bills and bank correspondence are addressed to the company; (vi) the VAT electronic tax system can be accessed from the premises. Quantified risk: for a low-risk, non-licensed consumer polling and market-research SaaS entity in a tier-1 city, the annual probability of an unannounced physical inspection by SAMR or the municipal tax authority is estimated at 5-10%; the probability rises above 20% if the registered address is a residential apartment or a shared virtual desk, or if anomalies are flagged in VAT invoice issuance.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Company Law of the People's Republic of China (adopted 2 November 1993; revised 29 December 2023; effective 1 July 2024), Articles 2-6, 23-26, 37-47, 46-48, 67-68, 78 and 83; Foreign Investment Law of the People's Republic of China (adopted 15 March 2019; effective 1 January 2020), Articles 2, 4, 11, 12 and 13; Regulations for Implementing the Foreign Investment Law (2019); Negative List for Foreign Investment Access (2021 Edition).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) and the local Market Regulation Administration at the municipal or provincial district where the registered office is located; negative-list consultation with the National Development and Reform Commission and the Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Company Registration (Filing) Application Form for Establishment of a Foreign-Invested Limited Liability Company, accompanied by the Articles of Association, the Joint Venture Contract, name pre-approval notice, and registered office proof.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum registered capital for ISIC 7320 market research and consumer polling services under the Company Law. The registered capital is set out in the Articles of Association and must be fully subscribed by the shareholders. The 2023 Company Law requires shareholders to pay their subscribed capital in full within five years from establishment unless a shorter period is specified or the State Council otherwise provides. No blocked escrow account is required by law; however, foreign exchange capital account proceeds are subject to SAFE actual-use supervision and may only be applied within the approved business scope.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS RESOLUTION OF [●] LIMITED

WHEREAS, the Company is a Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Venture limited liability company to be incorporated under the Company Law of the People's Republic of China; and WHEREAS, the shareholders intend to establish the registered capital, articles of association, banking, registered office and statutory officers at the first board meeting;

NOW THEREFORE, it is RESOLVED, by unanimous vote of all the directors constituting the first board of the Company, as follows:

1. Registered Capital and Subscription. The registered capital of the Company shall be [●] RMB, subscribed by the Chinese shareholder and the foreign shareholder in the proportions and form set out in the Joint Venture Contract and the Articles of Association. Each shareholder shall contribute its subscribed capital in accordance with the contribution schedule approved by this board, provided that the full amount is paid in no later than five years from the date of the Company's establishment registration as required by Article 47 of the Company Law. The Legal Representative and the Financial Controller are hereby jointly authorized to open capital contribution accounts, receive capital verification reports, issue certificates of contribution, and execute any instruments necessary to evidence the shareholding of each party.

2. Adoption of Registered Office. The registered office of the Company is hereby fixed at [address], and the Legal Representative is directed to file the documentation required by the local Market Regulation Administration and to record the office lease or ownership certificate as proof of a lawful permanent office. The Company shall pay all rents and operational maintenance expenses for such registered office out of the corporate account and shall keep at that office the statutory books, minutes, seal, and corporate records of the Company.

3. Banking Authorization. The Company shall open a basic deposit account, a general deposit account, and a foreign exchange capital account with [●] Bank at [●] branch. The Financial Controller, [●], and the General Manager, [●], are authorized to sign, singly for amounts up to [●] RMB and jointly for amounts exceeding [●] RMB, all checks, promissory notes, settlement documents, wire transfer instructions, foreign exchange purchase forms, loan agreements and any documents required by the bank. The bank is authorized to rely on this resolution until a written revocation is filed with the bank, and the Company shall indemnify the bank for all acts done in good faith pursuant to this resolution.

4. Statutory Officer Appointments. [●] be and hereby is appointed Executive Director and Legal Representative; [●] be and hereby is appointed General Manager; [●] be and hereby is appointed Supervisor; and [●] be and hereby is appointed Financial Controller and person in charge of accounting. Each officer shall exercise the powers provided by the Company Law of the People's Republic of China and the Articles of Association, and the Legal Representative shall be the sole person authorized to sign all documents requiring the corporate seal and the statutory legal representative signature.

5. General Authorization. The officers are directed to execute and deliver the establishment registration application, Articles of Association, leasing agreement, tax registration, social insurance and provident fund registration, foreign investment information report, company seal engraving application, and any other instrument or certificate necessary to carry into effect the above resolutions. No officer may act outside the scope of the approved Articles of Association without a further shareholder resolution. This resolution is effective as of the date of adoption and shall continue in force until revoked or amended in writing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Foreign-investment access screening, business scope design and name pre-approval
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) National Enterprise Registration Online Service Platform and local Municipal Market Regulation Administration; Negative List consultation with NDRC and MOFCOM
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Verify that the intended scope (market research, consumer polling platform, data analytics services) is not a prohibited foreign-investment sector under the Negative List for Foreign Investment Access (2021). Because the target entity is an equity joint venture, any restricted market-research activity would still be permissible only in that JV form and subject to the Chinese party's relevant shareholding or control requirement. Submit a name pre-approval application on the SAMR platform selecting the company type 'limited liability company (Sino-foreign equity joint venture)', propose 3-5 fully distinctive names, and define the business scope exactly to include market research and consumer polling without unauthorized trading or sensitive data-processing activities. The name notice is valid for six months, during which the subsequent formation filing must be made.
required_dossiers: Foreign investor certificate of incorporation and business registration (apostilled or legalized for use in China)
Proposed Chinese and English company names
Statement of business scope in Chinese
Power of attorney and identity documents for the name applicant
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If name is rejected, revise with alternative distinctive combinations and re-submit. If the name pre-approval expires, file a new pre-approval application. If the negative-list assessment is challenged, seek a formal written consultation from the local DRC and adjust the shareholding ratio or governance structure to meet the required Chinese-party participation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of Joint Venture Contract and Articles of Association and submission of establishment registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Market Regulation Administration (formation window) under SAMR; Chinese notary office or consular legalization channel for foreign documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare notarially or apostille-certified foreign investor resolutions and certified copies of passports and identity documents; execute the Joint Venture Contract and Articles of Association by authorized representatives. Submit to the local Market Regulation Administration registration hall or online portal. The application must be signed by the proposed Legal Representative, ratified by all shareholders, and contain the registered office, registered capital contribution schedule, board composition, Legal Representative designation, duration, and exact business scope. Include the lease of business premises with the real estate right certificate or building ownership certificate and lease agreement; ensure the address is not a prohibited or restricted use address. The Market Regulation Administration will review the dossier for statutory compliance and, if no error, issue the Business License with a unified social credit code, which is legal proof of incorporation in China.
required_dossiers: Foreign investor corporate/corporate documents and passport copies (apostilled/legalized)
Chinese investor business license and identity documents
Registered office lease and title/ownership proof
Appointment documents for directors, supervisor, legal representative and financial officer
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If SAMR issues a supplement or correction notice, respond within five working days with the requested documents and a written explanation. If the foreign investor certificate is defective, obtain a fresh apostilled or consularized copy and resubmit. If the application is rejected because of business scope inconsistency, execute a written amendment to the Articles of Association and resubmit.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-registration seal engraving, tax registration, and foreign investment information reporting
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Public Security Bureau (seal engraving recordation), local Tax Service of the State Taxation Administration, MOFCOM/SAMR foreign investment information reporting system, local Human Resources and Social Security Bureau
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After issuance of the Business License, within 30 days, apply to a public-security-authorized seal engraving enterprise to carve the company official seal, financial seal, legal representative seal, invoice seal and record the seals at the Public Security Bureau. Then complete tax registration at the local Tax Service, including taxpayer type determination, VAT general taxpayer qualification if applicable, financial and accounting system filing, and electronic invoice setup. Under the Foreign Investment Law, submit the foreign investment information report through the MOFCOM/SAMR online reporting system, disclosing actual and ultimate controllers, capital, industry and business changes. Complete social insurance and housing provident fund registration for employees.
required_dossiers: Seal engraving application and legal representative ID
Legal representative and supervisor ID copies
Employee information for social insurance and provident fund registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If tax registration is queried, respond to the tax authority within ten working days and file corrected information; if late registration penalties arise, submit a reasonable cause statement with supporting evidence. If the foreign investment information report is flagged, correct the data through the MOFCOM/SAMR portal and retain the correction receipt. If seal recordation is rejected, substitute the seal with a compliant engraving and re-file.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening RMB and foreign exchange bank accounts and injection of registered capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) through a licensed foreign exchange bank; People's Bank of China; commercial bank chosen by the Company
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Choose a licensed bank in China that is directly authorized to handle foreign exchange and open an RMB basic deposit account and a foreign exchange capital account. Present the original Business License, foreign investment information reporting receipt where applicable, Articles of Association, Joint Venture Contract, Legal Representative identification and corporate seal. Foreign exchange capital account settlement must comply with SAFE actual-use rules: foreign currency proceeds may be settled into RMB only for lawful business purposes within the approved business scope, and the bank shall review supporting contracts, invoices or payment instructions. The bank will report all account and settlement transactions to PBOC and SAFE. After receipt of capital, the Financial Controller shall obtain a capital verification report if required by the Articles of Association, lenders or the bank.
required_dossiers: Legal Representative and authorized signatories identity documents
Company official seal and legal representative seal
Foreign investor remittance instruction and SWIFT details
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If bank compliance rejects or holds the account opening, complete the enhanced beneficial ownership questionnaire and provide certified source of funds. If SAFE identifies a mismatch between the intended use of the remitted capital and the registered business scope, obtain an amended contract or authorized change of use and re-submit the settlement instruction.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate governance consummation, tax filing and annual reporting
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Market Regulation Administration, National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System, local Tax Service, MOFCOM foreign investment reporting system
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold a first shareholders and board meeting to ratify the Company's governance resolutions, confirm the constitution of directors and supervisors, approve the Financial Controller, and adopt minutes kept at the registered office. The officers shall ensure statutory books, seal and corporate records are maintained at the registered office. Execute monthly tax filings for value-added tax and enterprise income tax once the Business License is issued, file the annual enterprise report before 30 June through the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System, and submit the annual foreign investment information report through the MOFCOM system. If personal data processing is involved, implement Personal Information Protection Law compliance, including notices, lawful bases, data protection impact assessments and cross-border data transfer mechanisms, before launching the consumer panel platform.
required_dossiers: First board and shareholders meeting minutes
Tax return forms and financial statements
Foreign investment information annual report form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If an annual report or tax return is overdue, use the enterprise credit remediation window and file late with an explanation; if penalties are assessed, pay or contest through formal administrative reconsideration. If the foreign investment report contains errors, file a corrective amendment and preserve supporting documents. If the business scope is later found inconsistent with actual operations, apply to the local Market Regulation Administration for a scope amendment before further offshore remittances.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable - no manufacturing, chemical, assembly or warehousing operations under ISIC 7320; the business is a pure consumer polling and market research platform.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable - no industrial operating license or manufacturing permit is required; ordinary company registration, tax registration, foreign exchange registration and data-protection compliance are sufficient.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not Applicable - Ministry of Ecology and Environment would only become relevant if a physical construction project or industrial facility were later added.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - pure digital and consulting services; no Environmental Impact Assessment Report or Environmental Registration is required under the EIA Law and the Classified Management List for Construction Projects.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable - no wastewater, VOC or hazardous waste discharge is generated by the consumer panel survey platform; office-level compliance with municipal fire safety and electronic waste disposal practices remains the only relevant standard.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable at industrial level; no Civil Defense fire permit for industrial storage or chemical operations is triggered. The Company must still comply with ordinary office occupancy fire safety requirements under the Fire Protection Law of the People's Republic of China, including fire equipment availability, evacuation access and emergency planning, and with the Work Safety Law for any employees engaged in office-based operations.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration (STA) of the People's Republic of China (official web portal: www.chinatax.gov.cn) and the STA-managed Electronic Tax Bureau online taxpayer service platform (E-Tax portal)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Venture is a Chinese resident limited company; tax registration is completed through the national one-stop business registration data-sharing mechanism: (1) incorporate/register the JV with the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR); (2) upon issuance of the Unified Social Credit Code (USCC), the USCC automatically becomes the statutory TIN and the STA tax registration record is created through the shared data pipeline; (3) the JV must then complete supplementary registration in the Electronic Tax Bureau portal, including accounting standard, bank account, payroll, VAT taxpayer status, and foreign-exchange reporting particulars; (4) a non-resident foreign shareholder does not require a separate TIN merely to hold equity, but if it earns Chinese-source dividends, interest, royalties, or service fees, the local STA branch performs a non-resident withholding tax registration with the payer acting as withholding agent; the non-resident may also register directly under the non-resident tax registration procedure for refund/treaty claims.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. The PRC has no check-the-box partnership election or hybrid mismatch entity election. The JV is mandatorily an entity-level resident corporate taxpayer subject to CIT on worldwide income. Only administrative elections are available, such as VAT small-scale versus general taxpayer status and foreign-exchange settlement methods, which do not alter entity classification.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) under the PRC VAT legislation and the STA cross-border taxable services measures; standard VAT headline rate for market research/SaaS services is 6.0%, standard rate for physical goods is 13.0%, and eligible export services are 0%
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No turnover threshold for VAT registration: tax registration occurs automatically with the issuance of the USCC. Mandatory general VAT taxpayer registration is required when annual taxable turnover exceeds RMB 5,000,000; below that amount the JV may elect small-scale taxpayer treatment (levy rate currently lower, generally 1% or 3% depending on applicable policy).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: China mandates issuance of VAT e-invoices through the STA Fully Digitalized Electronic Invoice (FDEI) system under the Golden Tax Phase IV data architecture. Invoices must be generated via the Electronic Tax Bureau portal or an STA-approved API connection; each invoice receives a unique electronic invoice number and anti-counterfeiting QR code, and invoice data is transmitted in real time to the STA for fiscal clearing, input-output VAT matching, and cross-matching with customs and foreign-exchange data. Offline paper-invoice clearance no longer satisfies the general rule, and a non-compliant invoice may be denied as an input VAT credit.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: 0% VAT export treatment is available for qualifying cross-border taxable services; because the platform is structured as a SaaS consumer-panel survey platform, the service should be documented as software services or information system services supplied to a non-resident enterprise, performed and consumed entirely outside the People's Republic of China. Statutory conditions: (i) the customer is a non-resident enterprise/individual with no PRC establishment using the service; (ii) the service does not involve goods/property in China and is not consumed in China; (iii) the platform grants access from outside China with no China-market delivery; (iv) consideration is in foreign currency and repatriated through banking channels or a permitted cross-border payment institution; and (v) the service is classified in the STA catalogue of zero-rated software/information-system services. Standalone offline human-provided market-research reports or polling advisory may be VAT-exempt rather than zero-rated, so the commercial contract and delivery evidence must emphasize the automated SaaS nature.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Bill of Entry) and corresponding electronic customs declaration return for any physical survey devices, hardware, or printed materials shipped abroad; pure digital SaaS cross-border supply does not require a customs Bill of Entry

Bill of Lading or Air Waybill for physical exports; for pure digital services, retain server-access logs, IP-address evidence, and SaaS usage/consumption logs proving all service delivery and consumption occurred outside China

Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC) or SAFE bank foreign-exchange settlement voucher, including PayPal Mass Payout and Wise cross-border payout statements, evidencing actual receipt and repatriation of export consideration into the JV's China bank account

International service contract or click-wrap SaaS subscription order, in English or bilingual, identifying the non-resident buyer, service scope, SaaS licensing and delivery model, currency, price, and payment terms
STA Fully Digitalized Electronic Invoice issued as the export invoice, together with the VAT return and export zero-rating/exemption dataset filed through the Electronic Tax Bureau portal
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Upon audit, the taxpayer bears the burden of substantiating every export zero-rating claim. If the STA determines the zero-rating conditions were false, not properly documented, or the service was in fact used/consumed in China, it will claw back any VAT refund or exemption, re-assess output VAT at the applicable rate (6% for services or 13% for goods), charge a late-payment surcharge of 0.05% per day, impose a monetary penalty of 50% to 500% of the underpaid tax, and refer the matter for criminal liability under the PRC Criminal Law where fraudulent export refund or e-invoice fraud is established. The Golden Tax Phase IV system automatically cross-matches export customs declarations, VAT e-invoices, foreign-exchange receipts, and non-resident status, making unverified or fabricated zero-rating claims prone to immediate flagging and retrospective clawback.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE), operating under the People's Bank of China (PBOC)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: China operates a managed floating exchange-rate system; the RMB is conditionally convertible on the current account and only selectively convertible on the capital account. Current-account payments and receipts, including service trade and ordinary profit remittances, can be completed through a domestic bank on a real-transaction basis with contracts, invoices, tax forms and transaction-supporting records. Capital-account items such as FDI equity injection, external loans, and foreign-currency securities investment require SAFE registration or approval; conversion is transaction-specific rather than freely available. A Sino-foreign equity JV may open a foreign-exchange capital account and convert paid-in capital into RMB after SAFE registration, but the proceeds must follow the approved business purpose and cannot be diverted to prohibited sectors or portfolio investments. Export proceeds are no longer subject to mandatory surrender, and current-account foreign currency may be retained by the enterprise or sold to a bank voluntarily. Profit remittance to foreign shareholders is permissible once the annual financial statements are audited, taxes including withholding tax are paid, and the bank has verified the funds against the JV's tax and SAFE records. Cross-border data and consumer research services must also satisfy PBOC and cybersecurity data-export compliance before payment can be settled freely.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under SAFE regulations, there is no mandatory conversion ratio for export foreign-currency receipts; an enterprise may retain 100% of verified current-account export proceeds in a foreign-currency account or sell them for RMB at a licensed bank. However, export related foreign-currency revenue must be repatriated to China by the corresponding due date and generally within 180 days from the customs export declaration date, unless an extension is registered with SAFE. Service-export proceeds must be repatriated by the contractual payment maturity date, also within the 180-day verification window, and the bank will check the commercial contract, invoice, and service-trade declaration before settlement.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Foreign Exchange Capital Account (FDI Capital Account) and RMB Basic Operating Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Industrial and Commercial Bank of China Limited (ICBC)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Foreign Exchange Capital Account and RMB General Deposit Account for Operational Settlements
RMB Basic Account, Foreign Exchange Settlement Account, and Payment Services Account
RMB Basic Settlement Account and Foreign Exchange Current Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low and legally restricted for primary banking. Foreign EMI platforms such as Wise and PayPal do not hold PRC depository licences and cannot act as the JV's primary treasury or settlement bank. PayPal and Wise may be used only as downstream collection and payout rails after the JV holds a compliant domestic bank account, and any cross-border flow routed through them must still be declared and settled through a licensed domestic bank under SAFE rules. A China-domiciled entity cannot satisfy tax, capital verification, or SAFE reporting obligations by relying on an offshore EMI, so the onboarding viability of a fintech EMI as a substitute for Tier-1 domestic banking is effectively unusable.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is required for the entity opening process. The legal representative or a senior authorised officer with a valid notarised and consular-legalised power of attorney must generally appear in-branch for a face-to-face KYC interview. Remote consular proxy opening alone is not accepted as a substitute by most Tier-1 Chinese banks for the initial underwriting mandate, although the bank may permit the foreign legal representative to complete identity verification via a certified video interview in limited cases. For a Sino-foreign equity JV, at least one Chinese-operations principal, usually the financial controller or deputy general manager, must physically attend the branch with the company chop, board resolutions, articles of association, and the foreign shareholder's certified corporate documents before account activation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident shareholder structure with indirect ownership layers in unfamiliar jurisdictions creating uncertainty around ultimate beneficial ownership and source of wealth.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A complete ownership chart from the JV to every natural-person ultimate beneficial owner, current corporate registry extracts, certificates of incumbency, board resolutions, economic-substance evidence or tax residence certificates for each intermediate entity, audited financial statements, and source-of-wealth letters supported by bank statements and asset-ownership documentation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-frequency, small-value inbound credits from PayPal and Wise Mass Payout rails without clear customer identification, invoicing, or tax underwriting trail.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: The platform's AML and sanctions-screening policy, standard market-research customer agreements, respondent identity and consent records, geographic screening reports, transaction-frequency and value analytics, sample service agreements with major clients, aggregate merchant settlement statements from PayPal and Wise, detailed tax invoices issued by the JV, and reconciliation of gross revenue against SAFE service-trade reporting.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border intercompany payments for software licensing, data processing, or intellectual property fees presenting transfer-pricing, round-tripping, or false-service risk.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Intercompany licensing and technical-service agreements, OECD-aligned transfer-pricing documentation with benchmarking, SAFE service-trade registration forms, independent IP valuation report, withholding tax payment certificates, evidence of actual platform usage and data-delivery records, and proof that the IP has genuine business substance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Export or processing of consumer-panel survey data raising cross-border data-transfer, cybersecurity, and potential foreign-subscriber exposure issues not aligned with the declared market-research scope.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Data-security assessment report, privacy-impact assessment, network security filing certificate, cross-border data-transfer checklist with lawful transfer mechanisms, server-location and data-processor details, China consumer-protection consents, and a compliance opinion confirming that the survey activity does not touch prohibited data categories under PIPL, DSL, and MLPS requirements.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The JV must first complete SAFE foreign-direct-investment (FDI) registration and obtain the FDI business-registration information code. The foreign shareholder then initiates a SWIFT MT103 remittance to the JV's designated foreign-exchange capital account, with the remitter name matching the registered non-resident shareholder and with the transaction purpose coded as a direct-investment equity contribution. The receiving bank verifies the payment against the SAFE electronic registration, allocates the funds to the capital-account subsystem, and permits conversion into RMB only after documentary authentication. A licensed CPA must issue a capital-verification report for the JV, and the tax authority must be informed of the paid-in capital. Disbursement from the converted RMB capital funds is restricted to the JV's registered business operations and prohibited from entering securities, entrusted loans, or non-core speculative investments.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For service-trade outflows such as survey panel rewards, digital platform hosting, marketing services, and licensing fees, the compliant clearing rail is a SWIFT MT103 through a licensed domestic bank supported by the service contract, commercial invoice, SAFE trade-payment application, and withholding tax or tax clearance certificate. For physical trade in research materials or hardware, an irrevocable sight letter of credit or documentary collection against a full set of shipping documents is permissible and more appropriate for trade evidence. All outbound disbursements must be classified under the correct SAFE payment purpose code and pass the bank's post-transaction authenticity screening before release.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable CNY forward contracts and CNY foreign-exchange swaps executed with a licensed Chinese commercial bank against genuine current-account or registered capital-account exposure of the JV
Onshore European-style CNY foreign-exchange options for bona-fide cash-flow hedging of service-trade receipts and payments, not for speculative trading

Offshore RMB non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) executed by the foreign parent or treasury centre only, because onshore NDF booking by a PRC entity is not permitted, and these instruments must be backed by documented underlying trade or investment exposure
Cross-currency interest-rate swaps limited to duly registered onshore debt financing or loan liabilities, subject to SAFE and PBOC supervision

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Enterprise Annual Report (Annual Industrial and Commercial Report)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) via the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually no later than June 30 for the preceding calendar year; statutory filing window is January 1 through June 30
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: If the report is not filed by June 30, the entity is entered on the Abnormal Operations Directory within 10 working days; upon 3 years of continuous non-rectification the entity is escalated to the Serious Illegal and Untrustworthy Enterprise List, triggering public-credit joint disciplinary restrictions and, in aggravated non-compliance cases, administrative revocation of the business license by SAMR.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM) and SAMR through the cooperative foreign-investment information reporting system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on or before June 30 for the preceding calendar year; any substantive change during the year must be reported within 30 days of the change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or update the report is investigated by the investment authority; an order to rectify is issued first, followed by a fine of RMB 100,000 to RMB 500,000 for refusal to correct. Persistent non-reporting may also be integrated into national credit supervision records and can impair foreign-exchange settlement and subsequent corporate deregistration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Income Tax Annual Settlement and Filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Taxation Administration (STA) via the local in-charge tax authority
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on or before May 31 of the year following each fiscal year-end, accompanied by the annual financial statements and audit report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment accrues statutory overdue interest of 0.05% per day on the underpaid tax from the due date until full settlement. Underpayment, concealment, or fraudulent non-filing can trigger administrative penalties from 50% to 500% of the unpaid tax amount, compulsory enforcement, freezing of bank accounts, and tax deregistration; prolonged unresolved tax delinquency blocks the final administrative strike-off of the entity.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Statutory Annual Financial Audit and Audited Financial Statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Company shareholders and board of directors; audited financial statements must be submitted with the Corporate Income Tax Annual Settlement to the STA and retained for SAMR and MOFCOM inspection
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual financial statements must be prepared and audited in time for the annual shareholders meeting and no later than the May 31 corporate income tax annual settlement deadline for the preceding calendar year ended December 31
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to procure a mandatory CPA audit constitutes a breach of the PRC Company Law and Accounting Law; regulatory exposure includes a rectification order, fines against the entity and corporate officers, refusal by the tax authority to accept the annual settlement as complete, and risk that directors and legal representatives are held personally liable for false or unaudited financial records.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: There is no quantitative balance-sheet, turnover, or headcount threshold for exemption in mainland China. The PRC Company Law mandates an independent licensed CPA audit of the annual financial statements of every limited liability company, including a Sino-foreign equity joint venture. The audit is compulsory purely by legal form, not by size. A certified public accountant domiciled in China and practicing under the rules of the Chinese Institute of Certified Public Accountants must examine the financial statements on an annual basis.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: PRC Accounting Standards for Business Enterprises (CAS), issued by the Ministry of Finance and substantially converged with IFRS. IFRS as published by the IASB is not directly acceptable as the statutory presentation basis in mainland China. A Sino-foreign equity joint venture operating as a commercial market-research platform must apply full CAS in preparing the balance sheet, income statement, cash flow statement, statement of changes in equity, and accompanying notes.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under the PRC Foreign Investment Information Reporting rules, the joint venture must confirm its fundamental corporate information in the annual foreign-investment report filed by June 30. Any transfer of equity or change in actual controller or beneficial owner must be reported to SAMR within 30 days of the change. The national Beneficial Owner Information Registration framework likewise requires initial registration and 30-day updated filing for any change in beneficial ownership. There is no separate stand-alone annual UBO form, but the annual SAMR enterprise report constitutes the statutory annual confirmation of shareholding, actual controller, and control structure.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members, Register of Directors, Register of Charges/Mortgages, Minute Book

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% under Article 4 of the Enterprise Income Tax Law (EIT Law) for resident enterprises; non-resident enterprises deriving China-source passive income are subject to 10% withholding unless a treaty rate applies
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Small low-profit enterprises with annual taxable income up to RMB 3 million, total assets up to RMB 50 million and up to 300 employees pay a 20% statutory rate on 25% of taxable income, producing an effective rate of 5%; qualified High and New Technology Enterprises pay 15%; qualifying software enterprises can access 10% or two-year exemption and three-year half-rate holidays; R&D expenses are super-deducted at 200% (100% additional deduction). These incentives are strictly conditioned on substance and are not automatic for a passive shell shareholder result.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Annual Corporate Income Tax return in China is filed on the unified Enterprise Income Tax Annual Tax Return Form A (A100000), together with supporting schedules including A105000 (Special Tax Adjustment Items), A106000 (Loss Carryforward), A105080 (Depreciation and Amortization), A107012 (R&D Expenses), A109000 (Foreign Tax Credit) and A109010 (Dividend, Interest and Royalty Withholding Tax Items). Filing is performed through the State Taxation Administration electronic tax declaration portal (e-tax bureau).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; quarterly provisional income tax prepayment returns are required, and the annual reconciliation return is filed once a year after the fiscal year-end.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Quarterly provisional EIT returns must be filed within 15 days after the end of each calendar quarter; the final annual EIT return and tax balance must be filed and paid on or before 31 May of the following calendar year. Non-resident withholding filings must be made within 7 days of each withholding obligation arising, or on the due date prescribed by the local state tax authority.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Sales revenue from principal operations: revenue from consumer panel survey subscriptions, online market research data licensing and software-as-a-service platform fees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report all services rendered to, or consumed in, China on a gross basis. Reconcile PayPal Mass Payout and Wise receipts to declared revenue. Do not net out offshore service provider charges without supporting arm's length documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cost of sales and directly attributable costs of operating the market research platform.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Need pass-through costs for international sub-contractors to be supported by invoices or contracts. If a related offshore party is performing data analytics or panel recruitment, the charge must satisfy the arm's length standard and may be treated as a non-deductible cross-border royalty.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Marketing, administrative and platform operating expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Expenses paid to foreign related parties, including management fees, technology charges and cloud infrastructure costs, require contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation and may be disallowed unless the payee carries on substantive business and has beneficial ownership.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Other income including foreign exchange gains, refunds, government grants and non-operating income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Treat exchange gains from PayPal and Wise as ordinary taxable income. Any government grants not used for qualifying prescribed purposes are taxable; non-taxable subsidy qualification must be proved.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total accounting profit before tax adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use China Accounting Standards; if the joint venture's overseas parent consolidates under IFRS or US GAAP, GAAP-to-China-GAAP reconciliation adjustments must be reflected in the schedule.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Special tax adjustments: disallowed expenditures and transfer pricing upward or downward adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include deemed interest on thin capitalization, transfer pricing adjustments under Article 41 EIT Law, and disallowance of head office overhead allocations unless properly documented. For a non-resident parent receiving dividends, treaty exposure is not adjusted at this box.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax-exempt income, non-taxable income and loss carryforward offset.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only legally qualifying treasury bond interest and qualifying government subsidies are tax-exempt. Loss carryforward is strictly limited to five years from the loss year; no carryback is permitted in China.

This is the base for headline 25% tax. Any third-party or offshore financing re-characterized by the tax authority as dividend, interest or royalty withholding is not recognized here and triggers a Schedule A109010 WHT obligation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Income tax payable, foreign tax credits, and offsets for quarterly prepayments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A Chinese joint venture cannot credit taxes paid by its foreign shareholder. Credits are allowed only for the Chinese entity's own qualifying foreign-source income tax paid, supported by TRC and computation schedules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Withholding tax declaration for outbound dividends, interest and royalties.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Even though the JV is a resident taxpayer, it acts as withholding agent for non-resident shareholders. The annual reconciliation must attach full details of distributions, interest, royalties and the treaty rate claimed; failure to withhold under Article 37 EIT Law exposes the JV to a 50%-500% late-payment administrative penalty.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late annual EIT filing exposes the taxpayer to administrative fines of RMB 2,000 up to RMB 10,000 per return; unpaid tax is subject to a 0.05% daily surcharge; false filings under Article 63 of the Tax Collection and Administration Law trigger penalties of 50%-500% of the tax underpaid, and fraudulent underpayment or deliberate false declaration of non-resident withholding tax can constitute criminal tax evasion under PRC Criminal Law Article 201.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% under Article 37 and Article 59 of the EIT Law and its Implementing Regulations: a resident enterprise paying dividends to a non-resident enterprise shareholder is required to withhold 10% on the gross dividend amount, unless an applicable Double Tax Treaty or DTA provides a lower rate.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim DTA relief, the Chinese payer must first register the cross-border payment contract in the e-tax system within 30 days of signing or 30 days of the payment obligation arising, obtain and retain an official Tax Residency Certificate from the non-resident's jurisdiction, obtain a beneficial-ownership self-declaration and legal entity substance evidence from the recipient, and demonstrate that the recipient is not a conduit or shell company. The Chinese payer then files the withholding income tax return using the treaty rate and submits the treaty relief declaration to the competent Chinese tax authority before or at the time of remittance. If the recipient is determined not to be the beneficial owner, the Chinese payer must withhold the full domestic 10% rate plus interest and administrative penalties for incorrect declaration.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding tax on interest and royalties paid by a Chinese resident to a non-resident is 10%. Under the China-Hong Kong DTA, interest and royalty withholding is commonly reduced to 7%, and dividends to 5% when the beneficial owner is a Hong Kong company holding at least 25% of the capital. Other DTAs provide 5%-15% rates for interest and 5%-10% for royalties depending on the counterparty; all treaty claims require a current Tax Residency Certificate, CIGA analysis and beneficial-ownership evidence.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation (Local File) is statutorily triggered when related-party annual tangible property transfers exceed RMB 200 million, intangible property transfers exceed RMB 100 million, financial asset transfers exceed RMB 100 million, or other related-party transactions exceed RMB 40 million. A Master File is required when the multinational group's annual related-party transaction value is materially above the State Taxation Administration threshold, and Country-by-Country Reporting is required when the consolidated group revenue equals or exceeds RMB 5.5 billion; the Chinese JV should nonetheless prepare arm's length documentation even below the thresholds if any cross-border intercompany transaction exists because China permits the tax authority to scrutinize any related-party arrangement.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Although China does not apply a Gulf-style Economic Substance Regulations code, the State Taxation Administration applies a substance-over-form doctrine and the General Anti-Avoidance Rule (GAAR) under EIT Law Article 47 to disregard a structure that has no substantial commercial justifiability. For DTA benefits, the Chinese tax authority applies a Core Income-Generating Activities (CIGA) and beneficial-ownership test; an offshore affiliate receiving royalties, dividends or survey-data fees must show management decision-making, employees, risk exposure and real operational activity in its tax-residency jurisdiction. A shell entity interposed solely between the Chinese JV and its end customer will be denied treaty benefits and its payments will be taxed as China-source income.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion and Fraudulent Cross-Border Revenue Under-Reporting
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately omitting or shifting inbound consumer-panel survey revenue received through PayPal Mass Payout and Wise to an offshore affiliated collecting account, under-declaring the Chinese JV's SaaS subscription and licensing income, or backdating contracts to avoid recognizing China-source revenue in the correct fiscal year.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax Collection and Administration Law Article 63 imposes a penalty of 50%-500% of the unpaid tax plus daily interest at 0.05%; PRC Criminal Law Article 201 punses fraudulent failure to file or false filing of tax returns; if the amount of tax evaded exceeds RMB 50,000 and is more than 10% of the tax payable, the criminal penalty is imprisonment of up to three years and a fine, and for very large amounts, imprisonment from three to seven years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Under PRC Company Law Article 20, a controlling shareholder or director who abuses the corporate limited-liability form to evade tax is jointly and severally liable to creditors for the unpaid tax and losses. Where the offending director is the actual controller, the competent tax authority may list the individual on the serious-tax-violation information disclosure system, impose exit and travel restrictions under the Administration of Exit and Entry Law, and a criminal conviction triggers mandatory travel bans, asset freezing and confiscation of personal assets used to conceal the fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Manipulation and Thin Capitalization Through Offshore Service Fees
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The Chinese JV enters into intercompany contracts with its non-resident joint-venture partner or survey technology parent under which it pays disproportionate royalties, data-access charges, cloud hosting fees or management charges without performing any actual personnel, research, development, risk-taking or decision-making functions in China, thereby stripping taxable profit out of the mainland.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: EIT Law Articles 41, 46, 47 and 48 and the State Taxation Administration's Transfer Pricing Measures authorize the tax authority to re-characterize the payments, deny deductions, impute interest and make a transfer pricing adjustment; the additional tax may be subject to interest computed from the due date plus an added special tax adjustment interest of 5 percentage points where contemporaneous documentation is not provided. Article 102 of the Tax Collection and Administration Law permits priority seizure and collection from bank deposits for the adjusted tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: If the director or financial controller signs non-arm's length intercompany agreements that cause the Chinese JV to default on statutory tax obligations, Chinese courts can pierce the corporate veil and hold the director personally liable for the adjusted tax, interest and penalties. A foreign director whose personal assets are outside China is nonetheless subject to cross-border civil recognition and enforcement, an Interpol red notice or court-ordered travel restrictions, and if fraudulent falsification of invoices or documentation is established, the director is additionally exposed to criminal liability under Criminal Law Article 205 for false invoicing, with imprisonment up to life in serious cases.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company Status and Abusive DTA Claim / AML Red Flag
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The non-resident shareholder or an intermediate holding company is a tax-haven shell with no real office, employees, bank management, decision-making or core income-generating activity, yet it claims reduced withholding treaty rates on dividends, interest and royalties paid by the Chinese JV; the JV also forms interposed entities simply to route funds through PayPal and Wise while disguising economically condemnable Chinese business operations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under EIT Law Article 47 and the Implementation Regulations, the State Taxation Administration may disregard the abusive arrangement and re-source the income to China at a 10% withholding rate or a worse domestic deemed-profit rate. The PRC Anti-Money Laundering Law and cross-border foreign exchange rules impose substantial fines on financial institutions and payment intermediaries processing disguised transactions, and the relevant regulatory regulator may blacklist the entity; repeated violations trigger revocation of the platform's payment-channel approvals and administrative penalties up to RMB 1 million or higher for institutions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors approving the fraudulent treaty claim or money transfers are personally exposed to civil claw-back actions for tax shortfalls; the corporate veil is pierced for having used the shell entity as a sham instrumentality, and directors face criminal sanctions for intentional non-payment, forgery of tax residency certificates or participation in tax-related money laundering, including imprisonment ranging from five to ten years for aggravated money laundering under PRC Criminal Law Article 191. The director's travel rights may be suspended by administrative blacklisting until the tax liability and penalties are settled.
